exercises.prompt: How does changing the preposition alter the meaning of رَغِبَ?
choices: رَغِبَ فِي = 'to desire'; رَغِبَ عَنْ = 'to turn away from / dislike'
رَغِبَ فِي = 'to dislike'; رَغِبَ عَنْ = 'to desire'
exercises.answer: رَغِبَ فِي = 'to desire'; رَغِبَ عَنْ = 'to turn away from / dislike'
exercises.explanation: Classical Arabic verbs frequently shift or invert meaning depending on the governing preposition.

feedback.rule: Verb–preposition idioms: رَغِبَ فِي (desire) vs. رَغِبَ عَنْ (shun).

exercises.prompt: Identify the case of أَمَامَ and المُعَلِّمِ in جَلَسَ الطَّالِبُ أَمَامَ المُعَلِّمِ:
choices: أَمَامَ = Accusative ẓarf (muḍāf); المُعَلِّمِ = Genitive muḍāf ilayh
exercises.answer: أَمَامَ = Accusative ẓarf (muḍāf); المُعَلِّمِ = Genitive muḍāf ilayh
exercises.explanation: Locative nouns (ẓurūf) take the adverbial accusative and annex the following noun in the genitive.
